reviews.text:
Journal, habit tracker, goal tracking, project manager..... Update 3: 6/3/25 Yep. Still love it. How easy is it to start a journal and save oil change and tires rotated today, mileage x,xxx. Or changed HVAC filter 6/3/25, and when you want to see your history of oil changes just search from the main page. Or you could make trackers for car, home, etc maintenance and set recurring alerts, the possibilities are nearly limitless. Add in the numerical tracking and easy visual graphing and it’s that much better. I sound like a commercial but no one asked me for this and I pay for it annually, just letting you know. 

Update 2: 12/7/2017 Still loving app. And still finding new ways to use it. Over and over I’ll find myself using a special purpose app and realize - I can do this in Lumen. A great way to simplify life. I’ve also learned to move anything I’m not using into an archive file. It’s almost a sure thing that I’ll think of something again later that I want to track, focus on etc and it’s nice to just pull it back into my daily workflow out my archive file. 
Update : still loving Lumen Trails. Been using for years and is the among the very best money I spend at $9.99/yr. 
** Do like the ideas iamlmg7 has and would love to see them. Simple is good, but a little customization like background colors and ability to highlight certain lists would be awesome and while I haven’t deleted any info by accident yet, it would be too easy to do so. So maybe a lock feature, or at least a trash bin from which data could be recovered if deleted accidentally. 

From a daily journal - with pics, voice memos, location - anything combo you want to add - to a simple grocery list - this thing is super powerful, and unbelievably simple at the same time - just buy, play with it, check out the screen shots on all the different editions for ideas. Create folders - personal, work, etc. inside create a folder for each project you have - then a check list or list we colored bubbles with each action item needed. Make a folder for habits - then yes/no, number value (with or without additive and/or cumulative properties), general number or dollars, to track habits - or anything. Charting makes easy to see trends. Can search for anything and stays perfectly synced between iPhone and iPad. So many uses, it really is like 10 apps on one ! Buy it ! You will be glad !

First, this is the best general tracking app that I have come across, and one that I use on a daily basis. However, I have found several use cases that do not quite fit the built-in templates as well as they could. 
For example, I would like to track the level of anxiety I have on a day-to-day basis. It appears the best category for that is to use the Journal with Smileys. So let's say I have a very low anxiety day, I would naturally choose a more positive looking smiley face that represents I'm happy and not anxiety ridden. Yet tomorrow, I have very high anxiety, so I choose a frowning face to represent very high anxiety. 
I go along over the period of a month recording my levels of anxiety. Now when I look at the year view, it shows A graph of my levels of anxiety across time. Looking at a line or bargraph, I would naturally expect to see times of low anxiety to be represented with a low bar or line graph. Conversely, if I had a day of high anxiety I would expect the graph to Peak, showing a high bar graph relative to the low anxiety day.

However, just the opposite is true. The days where I have selected a happy face because I felt good and low anxiety actually graphs very high on the graph, whereas a day that I selected a sad face because I was feeling bad due to high anxiety the sad face actually graphs very low on the graph. So the result is if I have high anxiety it is actually going to graph very low on the chart, and if I have low anxiety, it will plot high on the graph.

There are many scenarios where the data graphs opposite of where one would intuitively expect it to plot. Anytime you're tracking something that is essentially negative such as anxiety, stress, or pain those items are going to graph inverse to the way you would intuitively expect them to show up on a graph.

Used to be GREAT until.... I used this app for groceries, health stats, ideas, notes, journaling, you name it. This is many apps on one, really. They kept it up to date and bug free.

Had they actually updated the app (it's been the same for years) or created a newer version, I would consider buying another one-time buy. It probably isn't the type of app I would consider for a monthly subscription. The app is rather simple from a coding standpoint.

I no longer want to support this company. I may just delete the app now. Lumen Spark, you just lost a loyal customer.
